name: 52 cards
description: 52 Cards is a solitaire (patience) game related to Golf and TriPeaks: clear the layout by removing cards one higher or one lower than the waste. Full 52-card deck; single player.

overview.description: 52 Cards is a solitaire (patience) game related to Golf and TriPeaks: clear the layout by removing cards one higher or one lower than the waste. Full 52-card deck; single player.

history.origins: Solitaire related to Golf and TriPeaks; clear layout by matching cards one higher or one lower than the waste pile.
timeline: 20th century: Golf-style one-up/one-down solitaire becomes popular in American sources.
1989: Robert Hogue creates TriPeaks, a closely related one-up/one-down solitaire later popularized in Microsoft Windows collections.

setup.deck:
Deck type: 
Card rankings: Standard (Ace high or low depending on variant)
setup.dealing: Deal 52 cards in tableau formation per variant.

rules.objective: Clear the tableau by playing cards from the layout that are one rank higher or lower than the current waste pile card.
rules.gameplay: Deal layout; turn waste card; play from layout cards ±1 rank; clear all cards to win.
keyRules: Clear tableau by playing cards ±1 rank from waste
Play from layout only; one up or one down from waste

strategy.basic: Prefer moves that expose new cards; avoid blocking the waste.
strategy.intermediate: Plan sequence so high/low options stay open.
strategy.advanced: Track remaining ranks to avoid getting stuck.
tips: Golf/TriPeaks style; one up or one down from waste.

variations.name: Putt Putt
variations.description: Turning the corner is permitted: a King may be played on an Ace, and an Ace on a King.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Engine-level overrides for the Putt Putt corner-turning rule have not yet been modeled; rules are documented textually from sources.

variations.name: Queens on Kings
variations.description: Queens may be played on top of Kings to make the game easier.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Queens-on-Kings easing rule is described in text, but concrete engine overrides still need to be added for this variant.

variations.name: Wild Card
variations.description: One or both Jokers added to the deck and used as wild cards that represent any rank.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Wild-card behavior is described conceptually; engine overrides for adding jokers and treating them as any rank are not yet specified.

variations.name: Empty Foundation Head-Start
variations.description: The waste pile starts empty; the player may choose one exposed tableau card to move to the waste to begin.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Head-start rule using an empty foundation is documented, but engine progression and setup overrides for this variant still need to be defined.
